channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: PHP2Shell: an OpenAI model helped find the critical PHP flaws that triggered today’s emergency patches
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI says security firm Calif found one of two critical PHP flaws — CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, CVSS 9.2 — using GPT-5.6 Sol. A leak forced the PHP project to ship emergency patches today.

item.title: Recursive launches Flint, a laptop coding model largely built by AI — the first public test of recursive self-improvement
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Recursive, the startup led by ex-Salesforce chief scientist Richard Socher, has released its first model: Flint, a free Apache 2.0-licensed coding model that runs on a laptop — built in under four months, largely by the company's automated Eureka Machine research system.

item.title: NVIDIA DSX POD: the AI factory that ships in a box — 14 days from delivery to tokens
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA introduced DSX POD: complete Vera Rubin AI factories built inside modular containers and factory-tested before delivery — cutting deployment at a prepared site from six months to 14 days.

item.title: Anthropic turns Claude Security into a continuous scanner: findings tracked until the fix ships
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Anthropic's Claude Security now watches connected repositories as code changes, marks each finding fixed when the fix lands, and plugs into existing workflows through an API and MCP connector — in public beta for Claude Enterprise customers with $25,000 a month in launch credits.

item.title: Legora raises $550M at an $8.8B valuation: the legal AI arms race moves from assistants to agents
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Stockholm's Legora announced a $550M Series E at an $8.8B post-money valuation on October 21, 2026, led by Atreides Management — seven months after its Series D — as annual recurring revenue topped $200M and in-house legal teams became its fastest-growing buyers.

item.title: Make your coding agents talk across machines, encrypted: a hands-on guide to Reason Network
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Reason Network (reason-machines/reason-network, dual MIT/Apache-2.0 license, ≈893 GitHub stars in its first five days) is a small Rust daemon that lets coding-agent sessions on different computers see and message each other over end-to-end encrypted peer-to-peer connections. Your agents get MCP tools to list teammates’ sessions, send messages, attach small files, and ask a human for sign-off. This guide installs it, joins a second machine, and sends your first cross-machine agent message.

item.title: NVIDIA releases Kumo Forecast: a 340M open time-series model that checks the past before predicting
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: NVIDIA has released Kumo Forecast, an Apache-2.0 multivariate time-series forecasting model that pairs a frozen 340M-parameter MOMENT-1-large encoder with optional k-nearest-neighbor retrieval over historical data — and explains every forecast with horizon-by-horizon attributions.

item.title: Cellebrite's Genesis AI surfaces a confession from two years of jail calls in the Autumn 2026 release
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Cellebrite announced its Autumn 2026 Release on October 21, headlined by Genesis, its agentic AI platform for digital investigations. Investigators report finding nearly 8X more relevant evidence artifacts than manual review — from a murder suspect's confession buried in two years of jail calls to human-trafficking leads in 6,000 recorded calls.

item.title: Eternal’s Dark.ai: the Zomato parent bets on an AI assistant that ‘cannot read your conversations’
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Eternal, the parent company of Zomato and Blinkit, plans to launch Dark.ai — a privacy-first AI assistant running fine-tuned frontier open-weight models on its own infrastructure with end-to-end encryption — globally by the end of 2026.

item.title: CoreWeave's GTC Berlin double play: a six-layer Zero Trust AI Framework and one-command templates for robotics and AV
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: CoreWeave unveiled two things at NVIDIA GTC Berlin: a six-layer Zero Trust AI Framework that keeps customer keys, access, and model data under customer control, and Physical AI Launchables — one-command templates for Isaac Sim, CARLA, MuJoCo, AlpaSim, and Cosmos 3.

item.title: OpenAI's models are coming to Google Cloud: frontier models and Codex head to Model Garden
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI said Wednesday it will bring its frontier models and Codex agentic workflows to Google Cloud's Model Garden, with general availability planned in the coming weeks — putting its models on all three major U.S. cloud platforms.

item.title: NVIDIA unveils the OpenShell Reference Architecture: agents that think on Rubin, act on Vera, and are governed on BlueField
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: NVIDIA's OpenShell Reference Architecture, unveiled October 21 at GTC Berlin, is a full-stack blueprint for safe AI agents: models think on Vera Rubin, agents act on Vera CPUs, and BlueField-4 DPUs watch and govern them from outside the machine.

item.title: Stop burning tokens on grep: give your coding agent a local search engine with XERJ
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: XERJ (xerj-org/xerj, Apache-2.0, 12,600+ GitHub stars) is a single static Rust binary that indexes code, docs, logs, and PDFs for BM25, vector, and hybrid search — served to your coding agent over MCP. Its case study shows 2.7× fewer output tokens at the same solve rate. This guide installs it, wires it into Claude Code, and measures what it saves.

item.title: Databricks takes AI Runtime to GA: serverless GPUs for Lakehouse-native training, battle-tested on 100,000 GPU-hours
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Databricks on October 21, 2026 announced general availability of AI Runtime (AIR), its fully managed serverless GPU platform built into the Lakehouse — hundreds of companies including Robinhood, Merck and FactSet already train on it, with seconds-level launches, one-command starts and Unity Catalog governance.

item.title: Google Cloud's A5X brings NVIDIA Vera Rubin to the cloud: GA in November, 960,000 GPUs in the pipeline
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: NVIDIA and Google Cloud announced on October 21, 2026 that A5X instances powered by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 will be generally available next month, with Google Cloud planning to scale its Vera Rubin infrastructure to as many as 960,000 GPUs across multiple sites and expand availability to Europe.

item.title: LTM launches BlueVerse ValueMesh: an AI execution fabric for Oracle transformations
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: LTM announced BlueVerse ValueMesh on October 21, 2026, an AI execution fabric designed to help enterprises move beyond fragmented AI pilots and industrialize AI across the Oracle transformation lifecycle, from strategy and implementation to operations and continuous innovation.

item.title: Pigment raises $250M at a $2.3B valuation to make enterprise planning run itself
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Paris-based Pigment announced a $250 million Series E at a $2.3 billion valuation on October 21, 2026, led by the EQT-managed Scaleup Europe Fund, to push its AI agents from building planning models to running entire enterprise planning workflows end to end.

item.title: Workato hands Asia's builders its enterprise AI engine: free self-serve agents and MCP servers in Singapore
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Workato launched a free self-serve tier of its enterprise AI platform in Singapore at World of Workato 2026 on October 21, 2026, giving developers, students and small teams the same governed engine its largest customers use to build AI agents and MCP servers.

item.title: China Telecom and HKUST launch a joint AI-for-telecoms lab: research wired to a 304-terabit global network
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: China Telecom Global and the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology signed the cooperation agreement for a joint laboratory on AI for telecommunications on October 21, 2026, moving a strategic partnership inked in March 2025 into its implementation phase. The lab's first Scientific Advisory Committee meeting approved the first batch of research projects the same day.

item.title: Sandbox your AI agent in a branchable microVM: a hands-on guide to smolvm
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: smolvm (smol-machines/smolvm, Apache-2.0, 6,700+ GitHub stars) runs untrusted code in hardware-isolated microVMs that boot in under a second — and lets you checkpoint, branch, and rewind a running machine the way git branches code. This guide installs it, builds a locked-down sandbox for your coding agent, and packs the whole thing into a single portable file.

item.title: Text it like a friend: Sundae Bar's new personal AI agent takes tasks over iMessage, RCS and WhatsApp
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Sundae Bar AI PLC (AIM: SBAR) opened a beta of Sundae on October 21, 2026: a personal AI agent with its own computer, browser and persistent memory that you reach by texting it on iMessage, RCS or WhatsApp. The company says 150 beta sign-ups arrived almost immediately, forcing it to add capacity and open a waitlist.

item.title: Solcis launches Compliance Studio: an open compliance layer that checks every AI agent action against policy
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Solcis, a Singapore-based spin-out of 6clicks, released Compliance Studio and its Policy Engine on October 21: an open, self-hostable compliance layer that checks every AI agent action against policy as it happens and keeps a tamper-evident record for auditors. It plugs into NVIDIA OpenShell and Microsoft's Agent Governance Toolkit.

item.title: ElevenLabs launches Eleven Realtime: two speech-to-speech models for live voice agents
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: ElevenLabs released Eleven Realtime on October 20: two end-to-end speech-to-speech models, v1 Mini for natural conversation and v1 Max for complex tool-calling work. It shipped the same day as Mistral's Voxtral 3 voice-agent stack.

item.title: Gemini for government services: Google's five-part agent stack for U.S. agencies launches in preview
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google Cloud launched Gemini for government services in preview on October 20, packaging skills, secure connectors, and partner agents for federal, state, and local agencies. Missouri and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services are already trying it.

item.title: OpenAI acquires Orchestra Bio, putting AI agents in charge of drug-development grunt work
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI announced Tuesday it has acquired Orchestra Bio, a four-year-old San Francisco startup whose AI agents manage the operational side of drug development. The team and technology fold into Rosalind, OpenAI's life-sciences suite; terms were not disclosed.
